title: Degree and shifted-root norm of a prime cyclotomic field
statement: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $p$ be a prime integer. Let $\eta\in K$ have multiplicative order exactly $p$, meaning $\eta^p=1$ and $\eta^j\ne1$ for $1\leq j<p$. Let $E=\mathbf Q(\eta)\subseteq K$ be the smallest subfield containing the rational numbers and $\eta$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Then $E/\mathbf Q$ is finite of degree $[E:\mathbf Q]=p-1$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], and its field norm satisfies $$N_{E/\mathbf Q}(\eta-1)=(-1)^{p-1}p.$$ Here $N_{E/\mathbf Q}(x)$ is the determinant of multiplication by $x$ on the rational vector space $E$ [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant].

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 14.5, printed p.63 (PDF p.69), proof: minimal polynomial of the shifted primitive prime root and its norm.

proof.text: Put $x=\eta-1\in E$. Apply [lem-sfb-prime-root-shift-minpoly] in the characteristic-zero field $E$, where $\eta$ still has exact order $p$, to obtain its minimal polynomial $P(T)=\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}(T+1)^j$. In particular $P(x)=0$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 14.5, printed p.63 (PDF p.69), proof and its displayed minimum polynomial.

proof.text: Since $p\geq2$, the last summand $(T+1)^{p-1}$ is monic of degree $p-1$, and every earlier summand has smaller degree. Thus $P$ is monic, nonzero, and has degree $p-1$. Substitution of $T=0$ gives $P(0)=\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}1=p$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 14.5, printed p.63 (PDF p.69), proof and its displayed minimum polynomial.

proof.text: We have $\mathbf Q(x)=E$: one inclusion follows from $x=\eta-1\in E$ and the other from $\eta=x+1\in\mathbf Q(x)$. The polynomial $P$ proves that $x$ is algebraic. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-polynomial-quotient-field-iso] to identify $E=\mathbf Q(x)$ with $\mathbf Q[T]/(P)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] the latter has basis $1,T,\ldots,T^{p-2}$. Its image is a basis of $E$, so $E/\mathbf Q$ is finite and has degree $p-1$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 14.5, printed p.63 (PDF p.69), proof and its displayed minimum polynomial.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-field-norm-minpoly] to $\mathbf Q\subseteq E$ and $x$. Here $m=\deg P=p-1$ and $\mathbf Q(x)=E$, so $e=\dim_E E=1$, using the basis consisting of $1$. Consequently $N_{E/\mathbf Q}(\eta-1)=((-1)^{p-1}P(0))^1=(-1)^{p-1}p$. This determinant norm is exactly the norm specified in the statement, including when $p=2$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 14.5, printed p.63 (PDF p.69), proof and its displayed minimum polynomial.
